summary: Discusses the design of reliable multicast protocols that use negative acknowledgment, where receivers only speak up when something is missing. It describes goals, challenges, and a set of functional building blocks for such protocols. This is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3941.

eli5.summary: In a big classroom, the teacher does not ask everyone whether they heard. Only students who missed something raise a hand. This memo describes parts for building systems that work that way.

questions: what is nack based reliable multicast
subtitle: A toolkit of design pieces for multicast protocols where only receivers who miss data speak up.

tldr.problem: Sending the same data to a large group is efficient, but making sure every member gets all of it is hard. If every receiver acknowledged everything, the sender would be swamped with feedback.
tldr.mechanism: Receivers send a negative acknowledgment (NACK) only when data is missing, wait a random backoff time so that most of them can be suppressed by earlier NACKs, and the sender answers with repairs, preferably forward error correction (FEC) parity packets.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5401 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes the Experimental RFC 3941. It describes building blocks for protocol designers, not one complete protocol.

today: RFC 5401 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes the Experimental RFC 3941. The metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why NACK-Based Multicast
sections.content:
RFC 5401 discusses how to build reliable multicast protocols that use negative acknowledgment (NACK) feedback. NACK-based protocols generally need less frequent feedback than those based on positive acknowledgment (ACK), which helps with feedback implosion as the group grows.

The document is a framework of "building blocks", not a single protocol. It says it specifically addresses in detail three blocks not covered in other IETF documents: sender transmission strategies, the NACK repair process with timer-based feedback suppression, and round-trip timing used to adapt NACK and other timers. It also says implementations SHOULD use forward error correction as described in RFC 5052.

It started as the Experimental RFC 3941. The working group had stated its intent to resubmit it as a Proposed Standard, and this document is that update.
sections.eli5: Instead of everyone shouting 'I got it!', only the kids who missed something say so. That keeps the teacher from being buried in answers.

sections.title: Design Goals and Assumptions
sections.content:
Any protocol built from these blocks has to settle several questions, and the RFC lists them: the delivery service model, group membership dynamics, sender and receiver relationships, group size scalability, data delivery performance and network environments. The basic service model is bulk transfer, either fixed-size static objects or streams of indefinite length.

Scale is the main constraint. The RFC cites research suggesting NACK-based groups on the order of tens of thousands of receivers can work with acceptable feedback using probabilistic, timer-based suppression. There is a trade-off with latency: the delays that let suppression work also raise delivery latency and the buffering that senders and receivers need.

Receivers may be limited to unicast feedback, for example when multicast is restricted to a source-specific model. Any block for NACK-oriented reliable multicast SHALL be able to work without help from intermediate systems such as routers, although using such help when available is RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: A game for ten friends needs different rules than one for a whole stadium. The designers list the questions to answer first: how big is the group, how fast must it be, and what kind of network is it on.

sections.title: Sender Transmission and the Repair Cycle
sections.content:
The sender transmits data at a rate set by the application or, where congestion control is needed (REQUIRED for general Internet operation), by the congestion control mechanism. New data is multiplexed with repair data. Control messages from the sender may be sent redundantly, since positive acknowledgment is too costly for large groups.

The NACK repair process has four elements: receiver NACK initiation, NACK suppression, NACK message content and sender processing with repair response. A receiver starts a cycle when it detects it needs repair, and when FEC is used only once its needs exceed the FEC parity that is already pending for that coding block. It records the sender's transmission position when it starts, and later considers only needs up to that position when deciding whether to send.

The sender waits through an aggregation period to collect NACKs, then sends repairs, preferring previously unsent parity packets. Sending repair for the earliest content first lets receivers hold back requests for later content until the sender returns to that point.
sections.eli5: When you miss part of a story, you wait a moment before asking. The storyteller waits too, to hear all the questions at once, and then tells the missing parts in order.

sections.title: Random Backoff and NACK Suppression
sections.content:
To avoid a flood of NACKs, each receiver waits a random time before sending one. The RFC recommends picking these times independently from a truncated exponential distribution, so that most receivers hold off while a few early NACKers speak for the group. It gives a short algorithm, with C code, driven by the group size and a maximum backoff T_maxBackoff.

The maximum backoff is set as T_maxBackoff = K * GRTT with K >= 1. The RFC recommends the default K=4 when NACKs are multicast to the group and K=6 when they are unicast.

When the timer fires, the receiver suppresses its NACK if the NACKs it has heard (or the sender has forwarded) already cover its needs, or if the sender's position has "rewound" to a point before the receiver's lowest needed position, which shows the sender is already repairing it. Otherwise it sends a single NACK, truncated to the lowest needed content if it does not fit in one message.

Timers follow from the same value. The sender's NACK aggregation period is at least (K+1)*GRTT, its hold-off is 1*GRTT, and receivers use a hold-off of (K+2)*GRTT after sending a NACK.
sections.eli5: Everyone who needs help counts to a random number before asking. Whoever counts shortest asks for all of you, and the rest, hearing that, just stay quiet.

sections.title: NACK Content and Data Identification
sections.content:
A NACK names the sender and the object or stream that needs repair, then the FEC blocks or symbols required. With FEC, a NACK minimally identifies the coding block and a count of erasures (missing packets). A more efficient strategy has receivers name the exact symbols they want. The RFC's example is a code with 64 data symbols and 32 parity symbols, with symbol identifiers 0 to 95. A receiver with three erasures asks for parity symbols 64 to 66.

The rule is to request the lowest ordinal parity first, then the highest missing data symbols if parity cannot cover the loss. This strategy assumes codes such as Reed-Solomon where any parity symbol can fill any erasure. Since every receiver asks in the same consistent way, suppression stays simple across repair cycles.

Data packets are identified by fields such as sourceId, objectId, sourceBlockNumber and encodingSymbolId. A sourceId SHOULD be present, because packet source addresses are unreliable as identity (routing changes, NAT and firewalls).
sections.eli5: Instead of saying 'I lost some pieces', each kid names exactly which puzzle pieces are missing, using the same labelling for everyone. That makes it easy to see when two kids need the same thing.

sections.title: Timing, Group Size and Congestion
sections.content:
All these timers depend on GRTT, the group round-trip time, a conservative estimate of the worst-case round trip from a sender to any receiver. In the one-to-many method, the sender polls the group with a timestamp, receivers echo back a response, and the sender computes each receiver's RTT. If a receiver's RTT is greater than the GRTT, the GRTT jumps to it immediately. At the end of a probe interval it may decay to MAX(0.9*GRTT, RTT_peak).

The sender advertises GRTT to the group in one byte, using a quantization function. The RFC recommends RTT_MIN of 1.0e-06 seconds and RTT_MAX of 1000 seconds. It also says convergent operation does not depend on highly accurate GRTT.

The scheme needs only a rough group size, within an order of magnitude. Without any estimation mechanism, the RFC recommends a default group size of 10,000. Congestion control that shares capacity fairly with TCP and other reliable multicast is REQUIRED for general Internet operation, and the RFC names TFMCC and PGMCC as techniques that can be applied.
sections.eli5: Everyone needs to know how long it takes a message to reach the farthest kid and come back. The teacher measures it by asking and listening for the slowest answer, then tells the whole class.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Unlike unicast transport, one badly behaving participant can affect everyone in the group. A malicious receiver could send NACKs just to make the sender keep repairing instead of moving forward. NACK replay attacks are called out as a particular threat.

The RFC says it is highly RECOMMENDED to apply authentication and integrity checks, and that protocols built on these blocks MUST identify their approaches to security. IPsec authentication is RECOMMENDED, with the multicast extensions from the IETF MSEC working group. Protocols SHOULD consider their own replay protection when network-layer mechanisms are unavailable.

For large groups, shared keys for receiver messages keep the number of security associations practical, but they cannot identify an authenticated yet misbehaving receiver. The RFC suggests considering source-specific multicast (SSM) instead of any-source multicast, since SSM removes direct receiver-to-receiver signaling and gives the sender a central point for management. Implementations MUST also support policies to limit the impact of exceptionally poor-performing receivers, if acceptable for the application.
sections.eli5: If one kid keeps raising a hand for no reason, the teacher gets stuck repeating things. So the class needs a way to check who is really in it and to stop troublemakers.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 3941
sections.content:
The RFC lists three differences from the Experimental RFC 3941: the title changed to avoid confusion with the NORM protocol specification, references were updated to related Reliable Multicast Transport building block documents, and the security considerations are more detailed.

Section 4 of the RFC adds that NACK-based approaches suit cases where building a higher-level unicast or hybrid delivery tree is impractical, and where broad fan-out over one hop is expected, such as cable-TV data or satellite. It compares the approach to PGM (RFC 3208), saying the NACK repair process can perform better than PGM when both run end to end without intermediate system help.
sections.eli5: This is the second edition of the rule book. It has a new title, updated pointers to related books and a longer chapter on keeping things safe.
